name: Cutting Off Hands
overview: The Scriptures use the metaphor of cutting off a hand to emphasize the seriousness of sin and the urgency of removing anything that causes one to stumble or offend. Jesus teaches in Matthew 5:30 and Mark 9:43 that it is better to lose a part of the body than to be cast into hell, highlighting the eternal consequences of unrepentant sin. This call to radical holiness urges believers to take decisive action against sin in their lives, valuing eternal life over temporary comfort or convenience. The passages in Matthew 18:8 and 5:29 further reinforce this teaching by extending the metaphor to other body parts, illustrating the comprehensive nature of the call to holiness.
